Title: Who reads this, and what should they do after reading it?
Detail_lesson: A board deciding a budget, a new hire on day one, a neighbour deciding whether to come. Name the reader and the action.
ClaudeNote: Write every section for the winning reader, and end with the action they should take.

Title: What do they believe today, before they read it?
Detail_lesson: Readers do not start from nothing. What do they think now, and what might they get wrong?
ClaudeNote: Start from the winning belief: agree with what is right in it, then correct what is not.

Title: How much time will they give it?
Detail_lesson: Two minutes on a phone, or twenty at a desk. It decides the length and the layout.
ClaudeNote: Size the document to the winning answer. Put the point first if the time is short.

Title: What is the one sentence we want them to remember?
Detail_lesson: If they forget everything else, this stays.
ClaudeNote: Make the winning sentence the title or the first line. Every section must support it.

Title: What decision or action should it lead to?
Detail_lesson: A yes, a signature, a change in how people work, a date in a calendar.
ClaudeNote: End with the winning action, stated plainly, with what the reader does next.

Title: What must it never say or promise?
Detail_lesson: A number we cannot stand behind, a promise we cannot keep, a name we cannot use.
CustomInstruction: One line it must not cross.
ClaudeNote: Treat the winning answers as hard rules. If a later direction would break one, say so first.

Title: What is the strongest argument against us?
Detail_lesson: The reader is already thinking it. Better to answer it than to hope they do not.
ClaudeNote: Draft a short section that answers the winning objection fairly.

Title: How would we say this in one picture instead?
Detail_lesson: A chart, a map, a before and after, a timeline.
ClaudeNote: Say how you would draw the winning picture and where it would go.

Title: What would the reader ask first, if we were in the room?
Detail_lesson: The questions people ask out loud are the ones a document should answer near the top.
ClaudeNote: Answer the top questions near the top, in the order people asked them.

Title: Which part did you have to read twice?
Detail_lesson: Look at what is on the screen. Where did you slow down?
ClaudeNote: Rewrite the top answer in plainer words and show it before and after.

Title: What is missing that a reader would need to act?
Detail_lesson: A date, a cost, a name to contact, a link.
ClaudeNote: Add the top answer where the reader needs it. Say where you put it.

Title: What can we cut without losing the point?
Detail_lesson: Shorter is kinder to the reader.
ClaudeNote: Remove the winning part unless it breaks a Keep in mind rule. Say what you removed.

Title: What would make a skeptical reader say yes?
Detail_lesson: Proof, a small first step, someone they trust saying so.
ClaudeNote: Put the winning answers on the Later list, and say which could go in before this is sent.

Title: Who should read this before it goes out?
Detail_lesson: Someone who will catch a mistake we cannot see.
CustomInstruction: A kind of person, not a name.
ClaudeNote: Add a review step to the Later list for the winning answers.
